simple.meaning: קוּן (qûwn) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to strike a musical note , i.e. chant or wail (at a funeral).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 8 times across 2 Samuel, 2 Chronicles, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, beginning at 2 Samuel 1:17. Its contexts include family, family line, kingship, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קוּן (H6969).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: קוּן (qûwn) / H6969 is traced through 2 Samuel 1:17, 2 Samuel 3:33, 2 Chronicles 35:25, Jeremiah 9:16 as a generated source-based concept entry.

structuredEvidence.definition: to strike a musical note , i.e. chant or wail (at a funeral)

firstOccurrence.englishText: David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son

timeline.evidenceText: David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son
The king lamented for Abner, and said, “Should Abner die as a fool dies?

Jeremiah lamented for Josiah, and all the singing men and singing women spoke of Josiah in their lamentations to this day; and they made them an ordinance in Israel. Behold, they are written in the lamentations.
I will scatter them also among the nations, whom neither they nor their fathers have known. I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them.”
In their wailing they will take up a lamentation for you,

“ ‘ “This is the lamentation with which they will lament. The daughters of the nations will lament with this. They will lament with it over Egypt, and over all her multitude,” says the Lord Yahweh.’ ”
